description: Baseline: default architecture, random init, prints the task object's public attributes.
2 layers, no LayerNorm, float64: hard one-cell-per-head attention gathers a; MLP forms partial products; second layer does long division on the remainder using emitted digits.
e02 with a single numeric output-digit slot; head logits c*d - c^2/2 are tangents of a parabola so argmax recovers d, dropping 8 slots.
e03 with partial products from numeric digit only: relu(A + BIG(d-m)) minus a token-embedded BIG*d(d-1)/2, removing the 9 thermometer slots and the b-cell gate.
e04 with one head reading a: scores log(10^(4-i)) make softmax weights the place values, so attention itself computes the decimal value of a.
e05 with one head summing partial products into P via log-place-value scores; answer digits still use one hard head each.
One head per layer, 10 slots: answer digits enter the same signed sum as the partial products, so a single softmax yields the running remainder on a known scale.
e07 with attention reduced to one scalar query/key/value (D->1, 1->D) instead of unused D x D projections.
e08 with per-block MLP width: 9 neurons for multiplication, 18 for digit comparison.
e09 with the query sign merged into KA, so one slot is both the query and key of layer 1 (9 slots).
e10 without a bias slot: KA is constant on every predicting cell, so it serves as the layer 2 query and the parabola constant (8 slots).
e11 with digit and a packed into one slot as BIG*d + a', so each multiplication neuron is simply relu(Y - m*BIG) (7 slots).
e12 with the output digit written on top of the shrunken remainder in one slot; the parabola head rounds the small fraction away (6 slots).
Negative control: e13 weights evaluated in float32. Tests whether float64 is really needed for a remainder of about 10^10.
e13 back in float64 with all LayerNorms present but neutralized: huge eps and gain leave x - mean(x), and zero-sum writers and readers cancel the mean (8 slots).
e13 with the 18 comparison neurons replaced by a third attention layer: a parabola score over a digit table in cells 0..9 selects floor(remainder / place value).
No MLP or ReLU at all: 4 attention layers read a and b, multiply through the bilinear score with a Richardson-corrected tanh, form the remainder and look up the digit.
Same model as e17, stress-tested on 300,000 random pairs plus edge cases, because its multiplier relies on floating-point margins.
Negative control on e18: multiplier uses tanh(s/2) alone, dropping the correction head's contribution, to test whether the cubic error matters.
Sensitivity test on e18: EPS2 raised to 1e-12, where the s^5 truncation error is predicted to reach about 4 on the largest products.

Sensitivity test on e18: EPS2 lowered to 1e-15, where rounding in the softmax weights is predicted to reach about half an integer of the product. Result: errors reached a few integers, larger than predicted.
Sensitivity test on e18: EPS2 of 1e-14, to find how far the working window extends on the rounding side.
Same weights as e13, stress-tested on 300,000 random pairs plus edge cases, with a count of nonzero parameters.
Boundary test on e23: BIG lowered to 1e5, which a + 1 reaches exactly when a = 99999, predicted to break a gate assumed to need a' < BIG. Result: still correct, because the gate only needs a' <= BIG.
Negative control on e23: BIG of 5e4, well below a + 1 for about half of all a. e24 showed the gate needs a' <= BIG, so this should break.
Sensitivity test on e23: BIG of 1e9, to find the upper end of the working window, where rounding of the BIG*d terms starts to matter.
Negative control on e23: SCALE lowered so SCALE/Z is below 1, which should make the step neurons inexact near digit boundaries.
Sensitivity test on e23: SCALE 1000 times larger, to find the upper end of its window, where rounding is amplified by the steeper step.

Negative control on e23: ballast on '=' removed, so the softmax normalizer Z swings from about 1e4 at the first digit to 1e9 afterwards. Result: R/Z swamps the digit sharing its slot, so the first digit saturates at 9.
Final model: 2 layers, 1 scalar head each, 6 slots, 27 ReLU neurons, float64. Layer 1 forms partial products, layer 2 does long division on the remainder; constants have wide tested ranges.
